get.summary: The server's clock, which the app pins its own to
get.description:
No token, on purpose: the clock is needed before the first sign-in.

The app counts this forward by the phone's uptime and stamps every offline
event from that, so a phone whose date is wrong -- common in the field --
cannot misdate a pickup, and the server's 72-hour window cannot turn a
correct capture into a STALE_INTENT.

post.summary: Log time spent on a receipt by hand
post.description:
The hour that was worked and never timed. Works offline.

Unlike the timer this one is *not* naturally idempotent -- two identical
entries are two hours -- so the capture-time ``Idempotency-Key`` is what
stops a retried flush from booking the time twice. Always send it.

get.summary: The customers a jangad can be posted for
get.description:
Every customer with a usable phone number, with their pickup addresses.

One record per customer (the commercial partner), never the company itself,
never a member of staff, never an archived record: the same people the
posting route will accept, so the phone never offers a choice the server
then refuses.

put.summary: Replace the item table of a collected receipt
put.description:
The whole table, as the office leaves it.

Rows with a ``move_id`` keep and update that line, rows without one are
new, and lines left out are removed. Sr follows the order sent, so the
phone's order is the receipt's. A replay therefore leaves the same table,
with or without a key.
